Title: Project Controls Specialists (all levels) - Performance & Reporting
Description:
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Please visit our website: www.turnerandtownsend.com





Job Description



Our PMO Midlands team is looking to expand its Controls community. We are a close-knit team and we’re looking to welcome passionate and ambitious candidates across all our professional, senior professional and managerial grades who will support our early careers, grow into leadership roles and bring their skills and expertise to our communities of practice, fostering our values with specific emphasis to Bringing out the best in Everyone.



With exciting growth in region including new Major Programmes, Projects and Clients, we’re looking for flexible and mobile Planning and Scheduling / Performance Reporting / Risk Management candidates to deliver services in our local region. Travel within the Midlands is required, dependent on the project and can be discussed further during the recruitment process. What you can give in flexibility and mobility you get back in access to diverse sectors such as Power, Water, Rail, Mass Transit, Local Authority, Shipyards, the opportunity to autonomously utilise your expertise to bring our clients bespoke solutions in response to their unique needs, and the opportunity to stretch yourself and boost your professional development with support from our network of dedicated line managers.



Working alongside project delivery teams as part of a wider reporting & performance management team or independently with reach back support to experienced performance & reporting professionals, responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following:



Tailoring reporting processes to meet the client’s needs and aligning with best practice.



Deliver to performance and reporting management plans for our clients based on project requirements, maturity, and best practice.



Promoting the benefits and requirements of Performance Reporting & Analytics within the project and programme team. 



Implementing, administering, and maintaining reporting systems and procedures to track project controls performance.



Working with the Integrated Project Team to establish a robust, integrated, well structured, accurate Performance Measurement Baseline (PMB) and support the change control process.



Roll out reporting calendars to ensure a consistent drumbeat of performance data and sufficient time to assure and analyse outputs.



Work with project controls to define requirements and data flows for information management systems and supporting our digital teams in their implementation.



Lead the development, analysis and maintenance of corporate datasets.



Provide guidance and advice on data quality issues to a wide variety of data providers.



Lead material preparation for governance through projects, programmes, portfolios and the enterprise.



Identify performance recovery recommendations for relevant stakeholders and management to support effective decision making.



Support the project team develop, embed KPIs and contributes to the development of the performance measures dictionary.



Developing project performance reports and dashboards, providing recommendations to relevant stakeholders and management to support effective decision making.



Lead preparation of presentations and other materials for client governance forums and performance reviews.



Contribute towards our national and regional performance & reporting communities including Communities of Practice.



Training and coaching clients and less experienced team members on performance and reporting management processes and practices.  





Qualifications



Experience in a project or programme environment is essential.



An understanding of how other aspects of Project Controls (Scheduling, Cost Control, Change Control) interact with Reporting.



Demonstrable track record in identifying reporting and data requirements and documenting these using the appropriate types of tools and documentation



Awareness of Project Controls software (Primavera P6, Active Risk Manager, Ecosys etc) is desirable.



Experience in using data analysis tools (e.g. Power BI)





Additional Information



Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.



Please find out more about us at www.turnerandtownsend.com

Colwick

We're working with a well-established business who are looking to appoint a Data Administrator to join their team.

Strong Microsoft Office skills, specifically within Excel.

Experience of working within an office/finance environment.
Able to communicate across a range of levels both internally and externally.




If you're confident using Excel, naturally analytical and have a keen eye for detail, we'd love to hear from you.

Title: Technology & Industrialisation Engineer
Description:
Manufacturing Engineer (Process, Equipment & Industrialisation)

Location: Sherwood, Nottingham

Construction has operated the same way for generations. We're changing that. Our vision is to transform construction through industrialised manufacturing—creating, proving and deploying technologies that make building safer, smarter, faster and more predictable.

At Laing O'Rourke, our R&D Manufacturing team is turning breakthrough ideas into real-world solutions that are redefining how construction is delivered. As part of the Technology & Innovation team, they sit at the forefront of the industry's evolution, accelerating the shift from traditional building methods to a smarter, more advanced future.

With the capability to create digital twins, develop bespoke production lines, trial emerging manufacturing technologies and test new products at scale, this is far more than modern methods of construction. It is the future of construction, being built today.

Behind every DfMA innovation lies a sophisticated programme of research, testing and validation. Working closely with our in-house design, digital engineering, manufacturing and delivery teams, the R&D Manufacturing team transforms ambitious concepts into scalable, industry-changing solutions that are shaping the next generation of construction.

Help define the manufacturing systems that will power the future of construction.

The opportunity

We are looking for a Manufacturing Engineer with a passion for industrialisation, production systems and advanced manufacturing. This is an opportunity to define how products move from design intent into scalable, repeatable production systems by balancing process, people, equipment, automation, logistics and digital technologies.

Working within our Advanced Manufacturing team, you'll help shape new manufacturing capabilities from early concept through to deployment, using engineering evidence, simulation and manufacturing first principles to influence how construction products are manufactured in the future.

Could this be you?

Do you enjoy solving manufacturing challenges by looking beyond individual processes and thinking about the whole production system?

Have you helped develop, industrialise or deploy manufacturing facilities, production lines or advanced production technologies?

Ready to apply your experience from advanced manufacturing, engineering or industrial sectors to help transform construction?

Key Responsibilities


Define manufacturing process architectures, production strategies and capacity models for new manufacturing capabilities.
Develop facility layouts and production systems that integrate people, equipment, automation and material flow.
Use simulation and digital manufacturing tools to evaluate and optimise production performance before implementation.
Work with suppliers, integrators and internal stakeholders to develop and deploy manufacturing solutions.
Support trials, commissioning and operational readiness activities.
Validate manufacturing performance using data, testing and engineering evidence.


Essential Skills And Experience


Experience developing or influencing manufacturing processes, production lines, cells or facilities.
Ability to translate product and demand requirements into practical production systems.
Experience of production system design, facility planning or industrialisation activities.
Strong understanding of capacity, throughput, flow and manufacturing performance.
Experience using digital manufacturing, simulation or virtual factory tools to support engineering decisions.
Ability to work across disciplines and challenge assumptions using evidence-based engineering approaches.


Desirable Skills And Experience (Trainable Or Transferable)


Hands-on experience or a degree qualification in Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent experience.
Experience with Dassault Systèmes 3DEXPERIENCE (3DX), particularly DELMIA for process planning, factory layout, simulation or resource modelling.
Experience of discrete-event simulation, robotic simulation, virtual commissioning or digital factory technologies.
Knowledge of automation, robotics, tooling, fixturing, metrology or advanced production equipment.
Experience of commissioning, ramp-up and deployment of manufacturing systems.
Exposure to high-volume, high-mix, configurable or first-of-a-kind (FOAK) manufacturing environments.


We welcome applicants from a wide range of manufacturing, engineering and industrial sectors who can demonstrate transferable skills in industrialisation, production system design, digital manufacturing or facility planning.

About Laing O'Rourke

Laing O'Rourke is an international engineering and construction business known for pushing boundaries in digital engineering, modern methods of construction and sustainable delivery. With more than 150 years of heritage, we are committed to creating environments in which diverse teams can excel and thrive.

We are proud to be part of the Disability Confident scheme. If you meet the essential criteria and would like to be considered through our Offer an Interview scheme, please let us know. We're also happy to provide reasonable adjustments throughout the recruitment process.

If you require an alternative format of this advert or need support during the application, please contact: resourcingteam@laingorourke.com

Title: Pricing Manager
Description:
Company Description

Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries.

Job Description

We're looking for a commercially minded Pricing Manager to join us in a highly visible individual contributor role, providing pricing expertise across a complex global business operating within a sophisticated matrix environment.

As a subject matter expert, you will lead and support strategic pricing initiatives across multiple markets, products, and stakeholder groups. You'll combine advanced pricing analytics, commercial judgement, and exceptional influencing skills to drive pricing maturity, shape pricing strategy, and deliver measurable commercial outcomes.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in complexity, enjoys challenging established thinking, and has a track record of delivering pricing transformation and commercial impact through data-driven decision making.

Reporting to the Head of Pricing & Insights, you will partner with senior commercial, product, finance, sales, and strategy leaders globally to ensure pricing reflects customer value, business objectives, and market dynamics.

What You'll Do


Lead complex global pricing programmes and strategic pricing projects, acting as the pricing SME across a broad portfolio of products and services.
Develop and implement sophisticated pricing strategies that optimise value capture, improve commercial performance, and support long-term business objectives.
Design and execute advanced pricing analytics, including price optimisation, segmentation, elasticity modelling, willingness-to-pay assessments, and commercial scenario modelling.
Build and apply statistical and machine learning models to improve pricing decisions, customer segmentation, and revenue outcomes.
Drive pricing maturity across the organisation through leadership of pricing change initiatives, frameworks, governance, tools, and best practices.
Influence, challenge, and advise senior stakeholders on pricing decisions, balancing analytical insight with commercial pragmatism.
Lead pricing experimentation programmes, including conjoint analysis, A/B testing, pilots, and market-based pricing studies.
Translate complex analytical findings into clear commercial recommendations for executive audiences.
Collaborate across global, cross-functional teams within a complex matrix environment to implement pricing initiatives and realise business value. Advise to commercial and product leaders, helping embed value-based pricing principles throughout the organisation.


Qualifications

Experience & Technical Expertise


Significant experience in Pricing, Commercial Strategy, Revenue Management, or Pricing Analytics within large, telecommunications, utilities, logistics, technology services, professional services, or other complex service-based organisations
Proven success operating within a global matrix environment, influencing cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority. Demonstrated ability to influence, challenge, and gain buy-in from senior leaders and executive stakeholders on strategic pricing decisions.
Hands-on experience building and applying advanced analytical models including regression models, cluster analysis, and customer segmentation frameworks.
Strong knowledge of statistical and machine learning techniques such as Generalised Linear Models (GLMs), tree-based and boosting models, regularised linear models, and Double Machine Learning approaches.
Track record of leading pricing transformation and change programmes that have increased organisational pricing maturity and delivered measurable commercial outcomes.
Experience acting as a pricing SME on complex global pricing projects spanning multiple markets, products, customer segments, and business units.
Deep expertise in value-based pricing, willingness-to-pay methodologies, price elasticity analysis, and commercial pricing strategy.
Experience designing and executing sophisticated pricing research and experimentation, including Conjoint Analysis, Discrete Choice Models, A/B testing, pilots, and demand modelling.
Proven ability to translate complex analytical outputs into clear, actionable commercial recommendations that drive revenue growth, margin expansion, and improved customer value capture.


Additional Information

Benefits package includes:


Hybrid working - 40% office based
Great compensation package and discretionary bonus
Core benefits include Pension, Bupa healthcare, Sharesave Scheme and more
25 days annual leave with 8 bank holidays and 3 volunteering days. You can purchase additional annual leave.

Manager, Strategy and Analytics

Manager, Business Analysis

Location: London or Nottingham, United Kingdom (Hybrid)

Working Pattern: 3 days in-office (Tuesday-Thursday) and 2 days remote.

Our Mission

We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. Throughout our almost 30-year history, we’ve consistently been recognised as a great place to work; in 2026, Capital One was officially ranked 9th in the UK’s Best Workplaces™ list. Hear from our team about what it’s like working at Capital One UK.

About The Role

As a Manager in Business Analysis within our UK Card division, you will bring strategic and quantitative insight to address high-impact enterprise challenges. Sitting at the intersection of strategy, data, product, and technology, you will lead key initiatives to design, test, and deliver strategies that support our customers and their financial wellbeing. You will thrive in a collaborative environment built on shared accountability, continuous learning, and innovation.

What You’ll Do


Strategic Leadership: Shape business strategies that deliver sustainable growth, customer value, and commercial success in a changing market and regulatory landscape.
Analytical & Credit Strategy: Deliver product-level modelling and analytics, enhancing credit performance by connecting future credit trends to historical data, refining risk models, and validating hypotheses.
Product Strategy: Design customer-centric lending products and implement effective pricing strategies.
Execution & Delivery: Sequence business intent, translate strategy into actionable technical and business requirements, and drive concurrent projects from concept to market delivery.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Partner closely with Product, Tech, Operations, Finance, and Risk teams to enhance quality, service, and commercial outcomes.
Marketing & Insights: Translate customer insights into clear go-to-market strategies, customer experience concepts, and direct-to-consumer marketing approaches.
Mentorship & Leadership Trajectory: Drive immediate impact as a senior individual contributor while mentoring peers, with opportunities to progress into direct people leadership as you scale your impact within the team.


The Skills And Experience You Need


Professional Experience: Experience in management consulting, financial services, or a quantitative strategy/analytics role, with a track record of translating analysis into implemented business strategies.
Analytical Problem-Solving: Strong quantitative orientation with a proven ability to pair conceptual thinking with analytical rigour to solve complex, unstructured problems.
Communication & Influence: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex data into clear strategic narratives and build alignment across stakeholders.
Inclusive Leadership: Experience leading projects end-to-end, guiding cross-functional partners, fostering shared accountability, and cultivating an inclusive team environment.


Nice To Have


Technical Aptitude: Experience with SQL or Python is a plus. If you bring a willingness to learn, we will provide the tools and support to help you build these skills.
Educational Background: A degree in a quantitative/ analytical discipline (e.g., Business, Finance, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science) or equivalent practical experience.


Where And How You'll Work


This permanent position offers hybrid flexibility based in either our London or Nottingham office.
We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.
Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. At our Nottingham head office, you'll find an on-site gym, restaurant and dedicated Learning Loft. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.
Cross-Site Travel: Approximately twice monthly to foster collaboration across both office locations.


What’s In It For You

We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.

Benefits

In addition to career development, our comprehensive benefits package is designed to grow with you, ensuring your wellbeing is prioritised at every stage of your career:


Wealth & Future: Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
Holidays: Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
Health: Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
Family Support: We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.


A full list of our benefits is available here.

What You Should Know About How We Recruit


We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.
We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.
Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices. Because each Business Resource Group is as unique as the population it serves, they offer a range of activities, networking opportunities, special events and learning programmes to associates.

Champion DevSecOps practices, CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code and cloud-native tooling to improve reliability, security and delivery efficiency.

Qualifications


Strong experience building data pipelines, data lake solutions or data platform capabilities.
Strong experience with AWS cloud services relevant to data engineering and platform delivery, including services such as AWS Glue, S3, Step Functions, IAM, Lake Formation, EC2, Lambda, EventBridge and SQS.
Strong experience with DevOps and Infrastructure as Code tooling, including Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, Git and Jenkins.

Experience with Configuration as Code principles and API integration.
Strong understanding of cloud security, data privacy, access control and governance principles in data platform environments

Knowledge of RESTful APIs and microservice architectures.
Experience working with sensitive, governed or regulated data environments.
Familiarity with data catalogue, metadata management, data marketplace or federated data mesh concepts.

Description:
Nottingham Trent House (95002), United Kingdom, Nottingham, Nottinghamshire

Lead Data Steward

Our Mission

We’re on a mission to be a force for good in lending. Throughout our almost 30-year history, we’ve consistently been recognised as a great place to work; in 2026, Capital One was officially ranked 9th in the UK’s Best Workplaces™ list. Hear from our team about what it’s like working at Capital One UK.

About The Role

Data sits at the very heart of everything we do at Capital One, and establishing a robust data foundation is a key enabler for our strategic initiatives across both the Enterprise and the UK division. With a multitude of systems capturing, storing, and processing data, our goal is to drive operations and analytics that help our customers and associates succeed.

As we scale up our AI solutions, ensuring a thorough understanding of the data the UK business creates and uses is more crucial than ever. This role is essential for maintaining a well-managed business, giving decision-makers absolute confidence that their data is available and of the highest quality. We are seeking an energetic individual to bridge the gap between data and the wider business, delivering well-governed, impactful data that drives real value for our stakeholders.

What You'll Do


Champion Data Governance: Act as the focal point for data governance and stewardship within the UK business, ensuring data is managed through its entire lifecycle and treated as a true corporate asset.
Support Data Owners: Manage day-to-day data activities on behalf of Accountable Executives and Senior Leaders who act as the designated ‘Data Owners’.
Enhance Data Quality: Drive actionable improvements to data quality and enrichment, focusing on the most critical data first and tracking the tangible ‘value-add’ with data consumers.
Ensure Compliance & Transparency: Maintain complete metadata, data descriptions, and lineage while ensuring data is correctly classified, protected, and compliant with GDPR and internal security protocols.
Manage Risk & Alignment: Engage with stakeholders to agree on common data definitions, whilst proactively flagging data risks or control issues to relevant risk and governance committees.


The Skills And Experience You Need


Stakeholder Influence & Collaboration: Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with a proven ability to influence across teams and drive cultural change.
Data Storytelling: Ability to translate complex data concepts into plain language, summarising information effectively and tailoring communications for diverse audiences.
Critical Thinking & Problem Solving: A natural analytical mindset with the ability to resolve complex data issues, identify trends, and take ownership of problem resolution.
Strategic Prioritisation: Ability to focus on high-value data tasks, piecing together data management practices to enable key strategic initiatives, including AI solutions.
Active Listening: Strong active listening skills to deeply understand stakeholder requirements and naturalise a data-centric culture across the division.


Desirable Experience


Data Frameworks: Familiarity with recognised industry data management frameworks such as DAMA or DCAM.
Data Modelling & Governance: Understanding of data governance principles, business glossaries, and how data flows via logical and physical data models.
Data Maturity Assessment: Experience evaluating data maturity and providing recommendations to align current capabilities with long-term strategic goals.
Technical Proficiency: Practical experience with SQL, particularly within Snowflake database environments.
Cloud Infrastructure: A general understanding of cloud resources, specifically AWS architectures.


Where and how you'll work

This is a permanent position based in our Nottingham office.

We embrace a hybrid approach to work. You'll spend three days a week in the office (Tuesday-Thursday), with Monday and Friday being dedicated work-from-home days.

Our offices are designed to inspire and support you. At our Nottingham head office, you'll find an on-site gym, restaurant and dedicated Learning Loft. Our London office boasts a rooftop running track and coffee bar.

What’s in it for you

We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.

Benefits

In addition to career development, our comprehensive benefits package is designed to grow with you, ensuring your wellbeing is prioritised at every stage of your career:


Wealth & Future: Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
Holidays: Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
Health: Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
Family Support: We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.


A full list of our benefits is available here.

What You Should Know About How We Recruit

We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.

We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.

Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices. Because each Business Resource Group is as unique as the population it serves, they offer a range of activities, networking opportunities, special events and learning programmes to associates.

Capital One is committed to diversity in the workplace.

If you require a reasonable adjustment, please contact ukrecruitment@capitalone.com All information will be kept confidential and will only be used for the purpose of applying a reasonable adjustment.

For technical support or questions about Capital One's recruiting process, please send an email to Careers@capitalone.com

At Capital One, we're building a leading information-based technology company. Still founder-led by Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Richard Fairbank, Capital One is on a mission to help our customers succeed by bringing ingenuity, simplicity, and humanity to banking. We measure our efforts by the success our customers enjoy and the advocacy they exhibit. We are succeeding because they are succeeding.

We believe that innovation is powered by perspective and that teamwork and respect for each other lead to superior results. We elevate each other and obsess about doing the right thing.
